# endInvocation

fun [endInvocation](end-invocation.html)()

Requests the current LLM agent to stop after the current step completes.

Scope is exactly this LLM agent: the per-step loop in [LlmAgent.executeTurns](../../../google-adk-kotlin-core/com.google.adk.kt.agents/-llm-agent/execute-turns.html) exits after the current step, and this agent's remaining after-agent callbacks (the checks at the end of [BaseAgent.runAsync](../-base-agent/run-async.html)) are skipped.

The flag does NOT propagate to any other agent. Enclosing workflow agents ([SequentialAgent](../-sequential-agent/index.html), [LoopAgent](../-loop-agent/index.html), [ParallelAgent](../-parallel-agent/index.html)) do not read [InvocationContext.isEndOfInvocation](../-invocation-context/is-end-of-invocation.html), and each child agent runs under its own context copy produced by `InvocationContext.forAgent(...)` / branching, so the mutation never reaches the parent's context. In `Sequential[A, B]`, a callback in `A` calling `endInvocation()` still lets `B` run. This matches Python ADK (`sequential_agent.py:91-99`, `loop_agent.py:113-122`, per-agent context copy in `base_agent.py:433`) and Java ADK (`LoopAgent.java:146` ->`takeUntil(hasEscalateAction)`, per-agent `toBuilder()` in `InvocationContext.java:270`). To break out of a [LoopAgent](../-loop-agent/index.html), set `EventActions.escalate = true` instead.

Mirrors Python ADK's `callback_context._invocation_context.end_invocation = True` and Java ADK's `EventActions.setEndInvocation(true)` / `setEndOfAgent(true)`.
